topics.title: Speed, Velocity and Newton's Laws
topics.subject: physics
outcomes: understand and apply the relationship between speed, distance, and time (u, s)
understand the terms: linear motion, speed, average speed, acceleration, and be able to investigate resistance to motion (u, s)
understand and apply Newton's laws of motion (u, s, v/a)

body.text: Speed tells you how fast something moves — the distance travelled per unit of time.
Velocity is speed in a stated direction. Acceleration is the rate at which velocity changes — how quickly an object speeds up, slows down, or changes direction.

On a distance-time graph, the gradient (slope) at any point gives the speed at that instant — a steeper line means a faster speed, and a flat (horizontal) line means the object is stationary. On a velocity-time graph, the gradient gives the acceleration.

Newton's first law says an object stays at rest, or keeps moving at constant velocity, unless a resultant (unbalanced) force acts on it. Newton's second law relates the resultant force on an object to its mass and acceleration.

Newton's third law says that whenever one object exerts a force on a second object, the second object exerts an equal and opposite force back on the first — forces always come in equal, opposite pairs.
